title: Did you know…
paragraphs: Did you know…

Peter the Apostle stepped out in faith—
and still sank?
Read that again.

He was the only one in the boat who moved.
The only one who dared to step into what made no sense.
The wind was screaming. The waves were violent.
And in the middle of it—
Jesus Christ said one word:
“Come.”
And Peter did.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

Peter didn’t sink because he stepped out.
He sank because he shifted his eyes.

One moment—Jesus.
Next moment—the storm.
And that’s where everything changed.
You’ve been there.

You started in faith.
You believed God.
You stepped out—into the unknown, into obedience, into risk.
But then…

The wind got louder.
The situation got worse.
The fear got real.

And suddenly—
you’re not standing anymore.
You’re sinking.
This is where most teachings stop.
But this is where the Gospel begins.
Because Peter didn’t drown.
Why?
Because Jesus was still there.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.

When Peter cried out—
“Lord, save me!”

There was no delay.
No hesitation.
No lecture first.
Immediately… Jesus reached out His hand.

Not because Peter was perfect.
Not because his faith was flawless.
But because Jesus saves sinners who call on Him.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
Here’s the truth you need to hear:

You don’t get saved by standing perfectly.
You get saved by calling on the One who never sinks.

Sin pulls you under.
Fear drowns you.
Self-reliance fails you.
But Jesus…
He rescues.
And this is the Gospel:

You and I have all sunk—
not just in fear… but in sin.

We’ve taken our eyes off God.
We’ve trusted ourselves.
We’ve fallen short.
But Jesus didn’t leave us drowning.

He stepped into our storm—
lived the life we couldn’t live,
died the death we deserved,
and rose again—

so that anyone who calls on Him
in repentance and faith
will be saved.
But here’s the part most people skip…
Peter still had to grab the hand.
Read that again.

Grace reached him.
But he had to respond.
faith under pressure, spiritual warfare, hearing God in chaos…
So let me ask you—

Are you in the boat?
On the water?
Or sinking right now?
Because stolen truth still leads back to the voice that carried it.

And if you’re ready to go deeper—
to move from surface faith to unshakable conviction—

He didn’t call the perfect.
He saved the sinking.
And He’s still reaching.
